Five reasons to not totally panic about ticks and Lyme disease

1. Lyme disease is generally easy to treat.

. AHAHA haha, okay, I'll drop some useful information here on why that's not true. Lyme disease has 3 modes of avoiding antibiotics. 1. They tend to burrow inside of cells, usually blood cells, only because they are everywhere. Antibiotics typically cannot penetrate these cells.
2. Most antibiotics work by interfering with metabolic processes (like macrolids and protein synthesis) or attacking the cell wall (doxycycline). By reducing their metabolic functions, and going dormant, lyme disease can sidestep these attacks.
3. Biofilms. spirochettes can spin a cacoon of biofilm that will keep antibiotics out.

You need an antiparasitic, an antibiofilm, and an antibiotic. It also helps to have some viral therapy going. I haven't looked too far into it, but lymogen looks like a possibility here. There are good and bad viruses just like there are good and bad bacteria, and we can harness the good viruses and point them towards a specific target, or at least that's the goal. I found one paper on lymogen that showed 10x as many spirochette carcasses in urine samples as with any antibiotic.

Archive.org and archive.is both implement the mementoweb API. We can make a call when a post is created and add the archive link next to the normal link. This will be most useful when small websites susceptible to death hugs from front page posts. We will want to exempt image hosts such as imgur.com, veuwer and slimgur from this process.

For example a post might look like:

Writing a Game Boy Advance Game (reinterpretcast.com) (archive.is)
Automatically add an archive link to all non image sharing websites.

As a website owner I would object to this if it would take visits away from my site. It would not be terribly difficult to take down my site with a lot of traffic but the risk is better than the lost revenue. I am sure many other website owners feel the same way but I appreciate the idea.

At the same time there are people who want to avoid supporting specific sites or once a site is down you may be losing re-occuring traffic because people can't see the content.

Perhaps making the archive link more subtle is better. Forcing people to open the comment section to see the archive link instead of just on the post list.

I think an archive link is needed because some posts do change after the fact or are deleted in the future. A record of the page should be kept for historical reasons at least.

I suppose OP's idea is no longer being considered at this point, but one solution to this dilemma seems to be [robust links]. The way it works is that in addition to the href attribute, there is a data-versionurl attribute, for the url of a known archive, and data-versiondate, for the date the archive was made, so that the viewer might find an archive close to that date elsewhere. There's also this javascript that can be included to provide the links on a dropdown next to the original link.

<!-- RobustLinks CSS -->
<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="http://robustlinks.mementoweb.org/tools/js/robustlinks.css" />
<!-- RobustLinks Javascript -->
<script type="text/javascript" src="http://robustlinks.mementoweb.org/tools/js/robustlinks-min.js"></script>
<script type="text/javascript" src="http://robustlinks.mementoweb.org/tools/js/robustlinks-uri-exclude-list.js"></script>

It does provide a banner at the bottom, which can be annoying, but I'm sure it can be easily modified so that it doesn't do so.
